suggested_requirements.text: The system shall receive configuration information from the EVLA M&C system and translate it into a physical correlator hardware configuration.
The system shall process and transfer dynamic control data and monitor data.
The system shall monitor correlator and correlator subsystem health.
The system shall take corrective action autonomously to recover from hardware and computing system faults.
The system shall provide tools to collect and display auto correlation products.
The system shall provide a Virtual Correlator Interface (VCI) for configuration via a human GUI.
The MCCC shall accept external data feeds for models, time standards, and fiber-link phase corrections.
The system shall issue an alert notice if a CMIB subsystem fails and does not respond to reboot requests.
The system shall automatically restart and configure a failed CMIB subsystem back into the operational environment.
The system shall activate a backup MCCC system automatically upon detection of a non-recoverable primary MCCC failure.
The system shall require unique identification for all users.
The system shall perform all login attempts in a secure manner.
The system shall provide an administrator with unrestricted access to all aspects of the system.
The system shall define access privileges for each user based on system access properties.
The system shall log all attempts to access the system.
The administrator shall have the ability to create, remove, and edit user access properties.
The administrator shall have the ability to block system access for users.
The interface between CMIB, MCCC, and CPCC shall be Ethernet of 100 Mbits/sec or better.
The interface between MCCC and external networks shall be Ethernet of 100 Mbits/sec or better.
The CMCS processors shall respond to correlator hardware interrupts in a deterministic fashion.
The system shall be self-monitoring and capable of detecting and reporting abnormal conditions.
The system shall be able to perform without total system restart between maintenance windows.
The system shall be able to continue processing configuration events until parameter queues are exhausted during communication loss.
The system shall provide a Graphical User Interface for test software to allow remote access.
The system shall use transformer-coupled copper twisted pair for internal network topology unless RFI constraints dictate otherwise.
The system shall use fiber optic or low RFI material for pathways penetrating the correlator shielded room.
The system shall provide a redundant serial communication path between MCCC and CPCC for remote reboot.
The CMIB shall be capable of reading a 16-bit identifier from the host correlator board.
The CMIB shall have an externally visible indicator for operational status.
All computers and peripherals shall be powered through UPS devices with sufficient capacity for safe shutdown.
Each computer system shall have a hardware-based watchdog timer to reboot the system in case of a hang.
